target_customer: Aspiring online video creators who pay to learn and monetize
problem: New creators struggle to grow an audience and earn money from their content.
business_model: Creator education and services (paid lessons and academy; exact model not confirmed by a company source)

founders.name: Kong Pham
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Founder/CEO; no background on the page.

founders.name: Jesse Jhaj
founders.background_notes: A single informal source says he left in mid-2016 (not verified).

founders.name: Peter Lu
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page as Founder/COO.

technical_complexity.rationale: A content education and creator services business needs video production and web tooling, not hard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Value came from the founders' YouTube creator credibility and instructors; lessons and courses are easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source opened shows what platforms or others did about creator education; unknown.

market_need_then: Online video creator careers were growing and Tubefilter's Aug 2016 headline says YouTube stars launched Jumpcut Academy to teach others (headline seen in search only).

branding.domain_note: Uses jumpcut.com; the name has been used by other companies, including a 2006 video editing site acquired by Yahoo.
branding.community_and_virality: Tubefilter covered the Jumpcut Academy launch in August 2016 (headline only seen).

brand_strength.rationale: The name is a video editing term shared by several unrelated companies, which confuses search, and no brand coverage beyond a launch headline was found.

outcome_analysis: Jumpcut raised a reported $2M seed in August 2016 from a long list of investors and launched Jumpcut Academy with YouTube creators. No later rounds, acquisition or shutdown were found for this company, and the YC page still lists it as active with 11 people, so the long-term outcome is unknown. A March 2025 Cinelytic acquisition refers to Jumpcut Media, a different company.
notes: Seed reported by StartupIntros (Aug 1, 2016) and Seedtable (Aug 24, 2016); both are aggregators. Other aggregator totals conflict ($370K, $291K, $7.25M) and are unverified; the $7.25M entry may belong to the unrelated Jumpcut Media. The company website returned HTTP 429, so it could not be read. No launch post on YC. Competitor list empty: a dated search found only undated alternative lists. Outcome search found no cause or event. Name origin not found.
